finding: A headless start through a .cmd/.bat harness shim now refuses any prompt holding a line break, a double quote, %, ^, &, |, <, > or !, instead of keeping cmd.exe out of the prompt's path.
why: A real task prompt almost always holds a line break or a quote, so on a Windows machine with an npm-installed harness (claude.cmd, codex.cmd) the headless kind fails every start while the probe still offers it; the cause (the prompt riding a cmd.exe command line) stays.
fix: Keep the prompt off the cmd.exe command line: resolve the shim to its real target, or hand the prompt to the harness through standard input or a file; keep the refusal only as a fallback when neither works.
evidence: headless.py:81 `BATCH_CUTS = set('\r\n%"^&|<>!')` ; headless.py:87-89 `if binary.lower().endswith((".cmd", ".bat")) and BATCH_CUTS & set(prompt): raise unavailable(... "use a prompt without them")`

finding: When the marker's body lines are no longer on screen, the footer-only splits still match the unchanged TUI footer, so agent-read returns no text with complete true and every new line is lost.
why: Splits with footer < real footer size use windows made of footer lines, which always match at the screen's end; before the delta a lost anchor gave complete false and the whole screen, now it reports caught-up: old=['a','b','c','+--+','| > |','+--+','? hint'], new=['n0'..'n4','+--+','| > |','+--+','? hint'] gives _after == 9 (len(new)), text '' and complete true (ran on _after/_marker, identical at 04c45c4); also with only part of the body scrolled off (new=['c','d','e',footer...]) the 'e' line is dropped.
fix: Accept a split's candidate only when its window holds at least one line above the footer that the new screen keeps as a suffix (e.g. require the rest/footer lines to match the end of the new screen and the window to sit before them); when no body window matches, return None so the read answers complete false.
evidence: herdr.py:407-414 `for footer in range(len(old)): window = old[max(0, len(old) - footer - MARKER_LINES):len(old) - footer] ... best = end + kept if best is None else min(best, end + kept)`

finding: _stop_without_tool is a near-copy of Herdr.agent_stop's kill block, and the copy has already drifted on its wait budget.
why: The same pid/alive/kill_tree/survivors answer now lives in two places with different wait_s rules, so a later fix to one stop path will miss the other.
fix: Move the shared kill-and-answer block into one helper (for example in process.py or contract.py) that both Herdr.agent_stop and _stop_without_tool call.
evidence: multiplexer.py:64 `survivors = process.kill_tree(pid, force=force, wait_s=min(20.0, deadline.left()))` vs herdr.py:315 `survivors = process.kill_tree(pid, force=force, wait_s=min(20.0, max(1.0, deadline.left() - 20)))`, both followed by the same `{"stopped": False, "reason": f"{len(survivors)} processes survived the kill", ...}` answer

criterion: Error and rollback paths, partial-failure handling
finding: Possible: on macOS `ps -o sid=` is not a keyword, so session_members answers [] and the orphan sweep silently does nothing while agent-stop answers stopped true.
why: The module targets non-/proc systems (creation_time falls back to `ps -o lstart=`), but BSD/macOS ps names the session column differently, and a failed ps gives empty stdout that the code reads as an empty session (unverified: no macOS host to run ps).
fix: Build the session list from `ps -A -o pid=` and os.getsid(pid) per pid, which is portable, or treat a non-zero ps exit as a survivor-reporting failure.
evidence: process.py:188-191 `done = subprocess.run(["ps", "-A", "-o", "pid=,sid="], ...) rows = [line.split() for line in done.stdout.splitlines()]`

finding: Likely: the creation-time filter also drops MSYS children, so a background child of an MSYS process that later exec'd is left out of the tree and survives agent-stop.
why: The id-reuse guard is needed only on Windows parent-id edges; an MSYS parent id is MSYS's own and maps to the current Windows id of that MSYS pid, which after `exec` is a newer Windows process than children it started earlier (e.g. `server & exec tail -f log`), so created(child) < created(parent) excludes them (inferred from Cygwin exec semantics, not run here).
fix: Apply the created(k) >= mine check only to children found through _parents(), not to those added from _msys_children().
evidence: process.py:203-204,219-220 `for parent, kids in _msys_children().items(): children.setdefault(parent, []).extend(...)` ... `queue.extend(k for k in children.get(current, []) if mine is None or created(k) is None or created(k) >= mine)`

criterion: Error and rollback paths, partial-failure handling
finding: A configuration file that cannot be read or is not UTF-8 still reads as no configuration, because afk-config.py crashes with exit 1, the same code as an absent key.
why: afk-config.py main catches only ConfigError, and load() calls path.read_text, so PermissionError or UnicodeDecodeError ends the process with an uncaught traceback, exit 1 (scripts/afk-config.py:404-409, 1482-1484); the docstring's claim that exit 2 covers a file that cannot be read is false, so a .afk/config.yaml with a Latin-1 byte and `transport.kind: headless` resolves the detected kind silently.
fix: Treat exit 1 with non-empty stderr as ConfigUnreadable (an absent key exits 1 with empty stderr), or make afk-config.py map OSError and UnicodeDecodeError in load() to exit 2.
evidence: probe.py:43-48 `A reader failure (exit 2: a file that does not parse or cannot be read) raises ConfigUnreadable.` ... `if done.returncode not in (0, 1): raise ConfigUnreadable(...)`

criterion: Error and rollback paths, partial-failure handling
finding: The dispatch timeout kills only the outer bash, so the verb's Python process keeps running (POSIX) or the timeout does not return until the verb exits (Windows), yet the answer says the verb 'was stopped'.
why: subprocess.run's timeout handler calls process.kill() on bash only (adapter.sh runs `bash "$dir/$entry"` and transport.sh runs afk-python without exec), and on Windows then calls communicate() with no timeout, which waits for the grandchild holding the inherited pipes (C:/Python314/Lib/subprocess.py:557-565); a late agent-start can therefore still open a pane and start an agent after the caller got exit 4, leaving an untracked agent.
fix: Start the dispatch in its own process group or session (Popen with start_new_session / CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP), and on timeout kill the whole tree (process.kill_tree on the bash pid) before answering; do not claim 'stopped' unless the tree kill left no survivor.
evidence: probe.py:137-140 `except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: late = {... "reason": f"{verb} on the {kind} kind ran past its {seconds:.0f} s limit and was stopped"}`

finding: No test covers the second half of the tab fix: a successor numbered from the highest number in use, not from the count of the step's tabs.
why: Reverting herdr.py:174 to `len(ours) + 1` still passes test_a_tab_name_that_ends_in_a_number_keeps_its_own_tab and the existing successor test at line 500, so the duplicate `<tab> 2` case the fix names stays unproved.
fix: Add a FakeHerdr case where the step's first tab is gone and `<tab> 2` is full, and assert the next start opens `<tab> 3`.
evidence: herdr.py:174 `label = tab if not ours else f"{tab} {max(_tab_number(t.get('label', ''), tab) for t in ours) + 1}"` ; tests: line 500 `fake.tabs["w1:t3"]["label"] == "goal step 2"` and lines 715-717 only

finding: A log that ends for good in a cut UTF-8 lead byte (an agent killed mid-character) never reads complete true; the marker stays one byte short forever.
why: _complete drops the trailing lead byte on every read, so end stays size-1 and `complete: end >= size` is false on each re-read from that marker: log ending b'...\xc3' gives text '', complete false, indefinitely.
fix: Trim a cut character only when the read stops at READ_CAP or the run is still alive; at the final end of a finished run decode the rest with 'replace' and answer complete true.
evidence: headless.py:58-60 `size = 2 if lead < 0xE0 else 3 if lead < 0xF0 else 4` / `return chunk if back >= size else chunk[:-back]`; 142-143 `end = offset + len(chunk)` ... `"complete": end >= size`

finding: With no usable tool and a handle but no pid, agent-stop answers stopped true 'nothing to kill' though the agent still runs in its unclosed pane.
why: A start whose process-info call failed returns pid None, so a later stop with only the handle reaches this path: {"handle":"w1:p2"} with herdr broken gives stopped true, method 'nothing to kill', pane_closed false, while nothing was killed.
fix: When pid is None and a handle is given, answer stopped false with a reason that neither the process id nor a tool to close the pane is available.
evidence: multiplexer.py:474 `answer: dict = {"stopped": True, "method": "nothing to kill"}` ... 483-485 `if handle: answer.update({"pane_closed": False, ...})`
